_comment: Sourced from Figma 'Lumen-AI-Design-System' file, page 'Design Tokens' > '02 Typography' (fileKey GJBYRm6ySR7XIECFcHMgy2, node 428:13769). Font family, as last read from that Figma source: Inter (UI text), Roboto Mono (code) — see the 2026-07-27 note at the end of this comment for a direct product decision that has since diverged from it, not yet reconciled back into Figma. H1-H6/Body/Label/Overline/Caption/Code map directly onto this scale's tiers: display-*=H1-H3, headline-*=H4-H6, title-* sits between H6 and Body at medium weight (Figma has no distinct 'title' tier), label-*/body-*/overline/caption/code-* are exact matches. button-* is a separate legacy scale read directly off the earlier Button page. standard-button-* was corrected 2026-07-29 via a fresh `get_variable_defs` pull on node 1034:4459, its first re-verification since the original sync: weight is SemiBold/600 (was documented as Medium/500), letter-spacing is exactly 0 for every bound tier (was a positive per-size value, 0.12-0.18px), and line-height now has exact bound px values — 18/22/28 for xsmall/medium/xlarge (was unset/`normal` for all four). `standard-button-lg` has no independent `Button/Large` Figma variable at all — the Large instance's own label node binds directly to the same `Button/XLarge` variable as the X-Large instance, so `standard-button-lg` is now 18px/28px, identical to `standard-button-xl`; this was a direct user decision (confirmed rather than inferred) after flagging the ambiguity. Also discovered during this pass: this component's real, live consumer is `AIButton` (`packages/ui/src/primitives/AIButton.tsx`) alone — the original hand-built `Button` primitive this token was named after was retired in favor of a shadcn-sourced `Button` with an unrelated size/type system (see `docs/shadcn-integration.md` §7.8); the 'Standard Button' name is a historical relic kept for backward compatibility, not a description of what currently consumes it. chat-message/chat-caption/chat-label (added 2026-07-26, chat-label removed then re-added 2026-07-27) are sourced from AIPanel (node 1079:3141) and the separate 'AI Conversation Components' documentation frame (node 1412:3030) via get_design_context's reported text styles: chat-message is the 'Body/Medium' style (Instrument Sans 16/18/400) used for bubble content; chat-caption is the 'Caption/Large' style (Space Mono 14/18/400, 0.2% letter-spacing = 0.028px at this size) used for the timestamp divider and response-metadata text (branch/edited); chat-label is the 'Body/Small' style (Instrument Sans 14/16/400) used for the 'Suggested follow-ups' section label that node 1412:3030's response-actions anatomy has (a section genuinely distinct from the in-bubble follow-ups the canonical 1079:3141 component uses, not a replacement for it — chat-label was briefly removed as apparently-unused before this distinction was made clear). None of the three exactly matches an existing tier at the same pairing, so new purpose-named tokens were added rather than reusing a coincidentally-close one, consistent with this file's existing app-*/ai-library-* convention. 2026-07-27: Inter and Roboto Mono were removed system-wide at direct user request ('remove both fonts'), independent of any Figma change — Figma was unreachable at the time (MCP disconnected), so this was NOT verified against or reconciled back into the Figma source, and the tokens below are now out of sync with the Figma-documented family names above until that reconciliation happens. `sans` and `brand` (previously Inter-only) now use Instrument Sans as their primary face instead, matching `interface`'s existing choice rather than leaving them with no named webfont; `interface` itself no longer lists Inter as a fallback behind Instrument Sans. `mono` (previously Roboto Mono-only) now uses Space Mono; `documentation-mono` (previously Space Mono with a Roboto Mono fallback) simplified to just Space Mono, since its only other named face no longer exists — then, once identical to `mono` in value, removed entirely (2026-07-27, user request: 'Can't we keep just --font-mono?') and its one consumer (`AIButton.stories.tsx`'s `font-documentation-mono` caption) switched to `font-mono`, since a second token with the same value served no purpose once the two families that once justified separate names had converged. Neither Space Mono nor Roboto Mono was ever loaded as a webfont via the Storybook Google Fonts import (confirmed: no `@import`/`@font-face` for either anywhere in the repo) — both always relied on the browser's own font matching/system fallback, so this change has no webfont-loading impact for the mono families. Instrument Sans's own Google Fonts import gained weight 700 (previously only 400/500/600) to preserve the brand-mark tokens (`app-logo`/`app-logo-compact`, both weight 700) now that they render in Instrument Sans instead of the Inter import that already covered 600/700.

input-md.usage: Input placeholder and value text, sizes md and lg (Figma Body/Medium). NOTE (2026-07-31): a fresh get_design_context pull on the canonical Input collection's own Size=md symbols (node 1262:1181) shows the real bound lineHeight is 26, not 18 — but this token is also consumed by five other components (`command`/`input-group`/`input-otp`/`select`/`textarea` internals), each with its own independently-tuned fixed height that a lineHeight change could visually break without checking each one against its own Figma source first. Left unchanged here (same 'flag, don't silently patch a widely-shared token' rule already applied elsewhere in this file, e.g. `_emptyStateComment`/`_contentStateComment`); the new `Input` primitive rewrite (2026-07-31) uses its own literal, correctly-sized classes instead of this token for exactly this reason — see `components/internal/input.tsx`.

chat-message.usage: AIPanel conversation bubble text (Figma node 1079:3141, 'Body/Small' style)
chat-message._comment: 2026-07-27 correction (user report: 'Chat bubble text font size is bigger in light mode, not aligned with the actual design'): this token briefly carried a light/dark fork (light 16/18 'Body/Medium', dark 14/16 'Body/Small') added the same day, on the theory that the two themes' canonical AIPanel instances genuinely differed. Re-checked both sides of that premise directly against get_design_context: the light value was never actually read from the canonical AIPanel instance (node 1079:3141) — it came from a separate 'AI Conversation Components' documentation frame (node 1412:3030) instead. The dark value *was* read from the real canonical instance (node 1166:4827) and was correct. Re-querying the canonical LIGHT instance (1079:3141) directly shows both bubbles at 'Body/Small' (14/16) — identical to dark. So there was never a real per-theme difference; only the light reading was wrong. Reverted to a single fixed value and removed the `dark` override (the per-theme typography machinery in build.mjs stays — it's generic, just unused for now).

ai-empty-state-title.usage: AI Empty Communication State heading, e.g. EmptyState variant="ai" (Figma node 1416:3638, 'Ask AI to get started', 'Heading/H4' style)
ai-empty-state-title._comment: Deliberately a new tier rather than reusing `headline-lg` (also documented as 'Figma H4', 32/42) — that token is weight 600 and is already a real, shared dependency of `KpiCard` in both the Angular and Web Components packages, so changing its weight would be an unrelated, unevidenced regression there. This node's own 'Heading/H4' text style, read directly via get_design_context, is weight 400 (Regular) — a real, narrower distinction, not a duplicate of an existing tier.

content-state-title.usage: ContentState heading, e.g. "No projects yet" / "Something went wrong" (Figma node 1174:1355, 'Heading/H5' style)
content-state-title._comment: Deliberately a new tier rather than reusing `headline-md` (also documented as 'Figma H5', 24/32) — that token is weight 600, while this set's own 'Heading/H5' text style, read via get_design_context and get_variable_defs on node 1174:1355, is Source Serif Pro Regular (weight 400). Same real, narrower distinction already recorded for `ai-empty-state-title` vs. `headline-lg`, and resolved the same way: `headline-md` is a shared dependency of other components, so changing its weight would be an unrelated, unevidenced regression there. letterSpacing is Figma's -0.5% resolved against this tier's own 24px size (24 x -0.005 = -0.12px); the build emits letterSpacing in px, so the percentage is not portable as-authored.

ai-empty-state-body.usage: AI Empty Communication State description text, e.g. EmptyState variant="ai" (Figma node 1416:3638, 'Body/Medium' style)
ai-empty-state-body._comment: Numerically identical to `input-md` (also 16/18/400, also sourced from 'Body/Medium'), but not reused — `input-md`'s name and usage are specifically about input placeholder/value text, and this is unrelated description-paragraph text; the existing convention in this file (chat-message/chat-caption/chat-label, ai-library-*) adds a purpose-named tier rather than reusing a coincidentally-matching one.
